summary.headline: Strides FY26 revenue rose 6.4% to INR48,587 mn and EBITDA 15% to INR925 crore at 19% margin; Q4 US revenue weak at $70 mn as flu season failed to materialise.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue grew 6.4% YoY to INR48,587 mn, held back by a weak second-half US flu season and donor-funding pressure in access markets; management says underlying growth was about 10% excluding access markets. Ex-US revenue grew 21% and reached about 50% of Q4 revenue, while EBITDA margin expanded 140 bps to 19% for the year. Q4 EBITDA rose 10% YoY to INR240 crore (18.1% margin), with about INR20 crore of logistics and air-freight cost pressure. Operational PAT crossed INR500 crore for the first time at INR518 crore, and the Board recommended a dividend of INR5 per share.

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue $284 mn and Q4 $70 mn, hit by a weak second-half flu season; 6 launches in the year, 9 products exited, and some molecules faced higher competition, with leading positions in 37 of 70 products. Controlled substances from the Chestnut Ridge ANDA acquisition are in their first full year, with 4 products launched and quota allocations below expectations.

segments.name: Ex-US (total)
segments.commentary: Grew 21% in FY26 and reached about 50% of Q4 revenue, with a 3-year CAGR of about 19%. Quarterly ex-US revenue rose from about $40 mn in Q1 FY24 to about $70 mn in Q4 FY26.

segments.name: Other regulated markets (ORM)
segments.commentary: Quarterly revenue rose from about $31 mn in Q1 FY24 to a $52 mn exit run rate in Q4 FY26, with traction in Europe, UK, Australia and the Nordics.

segments.name: Africa / growth markets
segments.commentary: Focus is shifting toward branded business, with Francophone Africa growing faster than the underlying market. The Sandoz product acquisition (announced Feb 2026) is expected to contribute from H2 FY27 and to lift the branded portfolio more than 1.5x.

guidance_outlook: Long-term aspiration: EBITDA margin upwards of 20% and gross margin in the 58%-60% range; Q&A reiterated a 18%-20% margin range for the near term.
US aspiration of $375-400 mn by FY28, described as a full-year FY28 target rather than an exit run rate; management said about 8 quarters remain.
Sequential growth expected from Q4 to Q1 FY27; Q4 sequential growth stated at 11% (14% excluding institutional business).
US growth expected to pick up from H2 FY27; FY26 seasonality was roughly 50:50 H1:H2 versus the usual 45:55.

Sandoz portfolio expected to contribute from H2 FY27; R&D spend to be $20-25 mn a year over the next 2 years; tangible and intangible investment run rate about INR300 crore; nasal sprays, patches and films expected to contribute mainly from FY28-FY29.
capex_capacity: FY26 total investment INR418 crore: INR236 crore tangible (including nasal spray capacity, ex-US capacity and a UK office) and INR182 crore intangible (global product rights and SAP HANA ERP upgrade).
Tangible capex is nearly complete beyond maintenance; a run rate of about INR300 crore across tangible and intangible is expected, including possible acquisitions of global rights.
Capacity sufficient for the next 2 years; no major additional capacity needed in the next 1-2 years apart from growth capex.
Chestnut Ridge facility (acquired from Endo) is capable of manufacturing nasal sprays and controlled substances; second nasal spray filed in May 2026, with commercialisation about 12 months away.
Patches and thin films: filing expected in 12-18 months.
demand_pricing: US flu-season demand did not recover in H2 as it had in prior years, and wholesaler discipline also contributed.
Marginal US pricing pressure, offset by COGS improvements; gross margin held in the 58%-60% range for 8 quarters.
Intense competition in a few molecules led to market-share rationalisation; management prioritises profitability over volume.
Q4 logistics and air-freight costs of about INR20 crore hurt margins; price increases are being negotiated with customers.
Access markets are facing donor-funding challenges, which management describes as tactical.

qa_highlights.question: What is happening in the US, including discontinuations and delayed launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the missing flu season, controlled-substance quota timing, and a policy of not launching until market conditions are attractive. It said 150 products are in the portfolio and launches will continue through FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Are controlled substances and nasal sprays structurally higher-margin, and how big is the controlled substances opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said controlled substances are an in-US-for-US strategy and margins will be similar to the current profile, not dramatically different. It declined to give revenue potential, saying the company needs more DEA quota first, and the company has gone back to the DEA for additional quota.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q4 SG&A and freight spike persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SG&A will stay around the current range, with Q4 freight costs elevated. It said a discount factor should be applied to Q4 when modelling.

qa_highlights.question: What are the nasal spray and new modality timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: One or two nasal products could launch earlier, but bulk revenue is expected in FY28-FY29. Patches and thin films filings are expected in 12-18 months, with about 5-6 additional third-party nasal programmes added.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sandoz deal's impact and the R&D outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The Sandoz deal is expected to close in H2 FY27 (October-March). R&D spend is expected to be $20-25 mn over the next 2 years.

risks_watch: US growth depends on a recovery in H2 FY27 and on the controlled-substance quota outcome from the DEA; no timeline was given.
Gross margin needs to stay in the 58%-60% range amid logistics, fuel, raw material and FX cost pressure.
Working capital: cash-to-cash cycle is 124 days, with inventory up 21 days and payables stretched in Q4, which management expects to normalise.
Competition in several US molecules and a 2-year wait before new nasal spray and modality revenue.
Access markets exposed to donor-funding challenges; Sandoz integration timing.
summary.management_tone: Confident on ex-US growth, profitability and balance sheet, but cautious and evasive on US timing, quota and controlled-substance sizing. Management repeatedly deferred US recovery to H2 FY27 and declined to quantify the controlled-substance revenue potential.
key_quotes: Ex-U.S. markets have emerged as the most important highlight of our performance.
We are reporting an operational PAT of INR518 crores crossing the INR500 crores mark for the first time.
We have not taken any exit run rate and all that.
I have clearly said that margins will be between the 18% to 20% range.
